Since, $K, L \in N$ possible values are $\therefore(K, L)=(2,2),(1,4)$

Consider the following statements (A) and (B)
(A) $\int_a^b \frac{d}{d x}(f(x)) d x=\frac{d}{d x} \int_a^b(f(x)) d x$
(B) $\frac{d}{d x}\left(\int f(x) d x\right)=f(x)+C$

Which one of the following is true?
questions.solution:
$\int_a^b \frac{d}{d x}(f(x)) d x=\int_a^b d(f(x))=f(b)-f(a)$ ...(i)
and $\frac{d}{d x} \int_a^b f(x) d x=\frac{d}{d x}[\mathrm{~A}$ constant $]=0$ ...(ii)
$\left\{\because \int_a^b f(x) d x\right.$ will necessarily give a constant value
Hence $\int_a^b \frac{d}{d x}(f(x)) d x \neq \frac{d}{d x} \int_a^b f(x) d x$
Therefore statement ' $\mathrm{A}$ ' is false.
Now consider

\frac{d}{d x}\left(\int f(x) d x\right)=\frac{d}{d x}\left(g(x)+C_1\right)

where $\int f(x) d x=g(x)+C_1$
\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow \frac{d}{d x} \int f(x) d x=g^{\prime}(\mathrm{x})+0\left\{\because \frac{d}{d x}(\text { constant })=0\right. \\
& =g^{\prime}(x)
\end{aligned}

Clearly statement ' $\mathrm{B}$ ' is also false.
